title: Dynamic Locomotion in the MIT Cheetah 3 Through Convex Model-Predictive Control
version: IROS 2018 accepted author manuscript from MIT DSpace; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2018.8594448
page_numbering: PDF pages, 1-based unless locator explicitly refers to printed page

claims.claim: 12 motion states plus a constant gravity state; control inputs are 3D contact forces
Convex model fixes future yaw and foot positions and assumes small roll/pitch, negligible leg dynamics and angular gyroscopic term
Stance force constraints are normal-force bounds and a square pyramid; swing foot forces are zero
Condensing X=Aqp x0+Bqp U gives H=2(Bqpᵀ L Bqp+K)
Experimental horizon 0.33–0.5 s, 10–16 steps, update 25–50 Hz, low-level state/swing/impedance 1 kHz
claims.conditions: Abstract separately summarizes 20–30 Hz and <1 ms solves; not conflated with all runtime settings

claims.claim: Text describes 45 kg robot, controller parameter table uses 43 kg
Real hardware forward speed up to 3 m/s; modified-leg-speed simulation 6 m/s
claims.conditions: Hardware tests on treadmill; simulation increases joint-speed limit to 30 rad/s; not hardware 6 m/s

claims.claim: Three reported stairs attempts include only one fully successful ascent/descent and multiple incidents
claims.conditions: Debris-covered stairs, increased swing height, proprioceptive sensing; not a large statistical success-rate study

claims.claim: Square pyramid inequalities are not identical to the Euclidean circular Coulomb cone; their corner reaches sqrt(2) μ fz
Learning-based residuals, contact schedule or friction prediction could interface with the QP, but were not tested in this paper
claims.locator: Reader synthesis; §VI motivates higher-level contact planning

scope_notes: All 8 official PDF pages read; no supplementary video quantitatively audited.
